forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Redcar and Cleveland applies for exceptional financial support after identifying £18.4m gap in 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council has applied to the Government for exceptional financial support, permission to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending, after identifying an £18.4m gap in its 2026/27 budget. The council's medium-term financial plan update of December 2025 identified the gap.

The council's external auditor sets out the application in its draft annual report for 2025/26, which is on the Governance Committee's agenda for 23 November. The auditor treats the council's reliance on exceptional financial support as an indicator of financial stress and as part of what it describes as a significant weakness in financial sustainability.

The report gives two other figures for 2025/26. The council's medium-term financial strategy of February 2025 forecast a surplus of £0.934m for the year. At the second quarter of 2025/26, the council forecast an overspend of £2.938m for the year.

findings.paper_title: 10.5 (11) DRAFT - Auditor's Annual Report 25-26 - Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council - For Issue
findings.headline: The auditor describes the 2025/26 draft accounts as received in June 2026 and of good quality.
findings.detail: The paper says the draft accounts were accompanied by an organised set of working papers, and that the auditor has encountered no significant difficulties to date.
findings.matters: A clean audit process with no significant difficulties to date is a point of comparison for finance teams preparing accounts under the same deadlines.
findings.quote: Draft accounts were received from the Council in June 2026 and were of a good quality.

findings.paper_title: 10.5 (11) DRAFT - Auditor's Annual Report 25-26 - Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council - For Issue
findings.headline: The auditor identifies two significant weaknesses in value-for-money arrangements, both under financial sustainability, and reports an unqualified opinion on the financial statements.
findings.detail: The two weaknesses relate to the DSG deficit and to Exceptional Financial Support. The audit report date is shown as to be confirmed, and the Whole of Government Accounts work has not been concluded.
findings.matters: Two significant weaknesses in one reporting criterion, alongside an unqualified opinion, is the audit position a finance director here or at a peer would compare against their own.
findings.figures: Two significant weaknesses; 2 recommendations (pages 25 and 26 of the paper)
findings.quote: We identified two significant weakness in arrangements.

findings.paper_title: 10.5 (11) DRAFT - Auditor's Annual Report 25-26 - Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council - For Issue
findings.headline: The auditor reports that the Council has breached its Capital Financing Requirement, and is working with officers to understand the reasons.
findings.detail: The breach was reported in the narrative report accompanying the draft accounts. The auditor says its work on the breach is ongoing and will be updated in the final Auditor's Annual Report.
findings.matters: A CFR breach is a treasury and prudential-indicator matter that lenders and peer finance directors would read as a question about borrowing headroom and compliance.
findings.figures: No figure given in the paper
findings.quote: The Council has reported in the narrative report accompanying the draft accounts that they have breached their Capital Financing Requirement (CFR).

findings.paper_title: 10.5 (11) DRAFT - Auditor's Annual Report 25-26 - Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council - For Issue
findings.headline: The refreshed MTFS identifies a £13.2 million funding gap over its life and a £5.6 million deficit in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper says the MTFS was refreshed in September 2026 and that the Business Rates Growth forecast has been reprofiled, so the additional income is now expected in 2029/30.
findings.matters: Pushing business rates growth income back by several years is a planning change that finance directors at councils relying on growth would weigh against their own assumptions.
findings.figures: £13.2m (funding gap over the life of the MTFS); £5.6m (deficit in 2026/27); 2029/30 (year additional business rates income now expected)
findings.quote: the revised plan identified a funding gap of £13.2m over the life of the MTFS, with a deficit of £5.6m identified in 2026/27

findings.paper_title: 10.5 (11) DRAFT - Auditor's Annual Report 25-26 - Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council - For Issue
findings.headline: The Council has applied to Government for Exceptional Financial Support to manage 2026/27 pressures, after identifying an £18.4 million gap in 2026/27.
findings.detail: The December 2025 MTFP update identified the gap. The auditor treats the reliance on EFS as an indicator of financial stress and part of the significant weakness in financial sustainability.
findings.matters: An application for Exceptional Financial Support, rather than a balanced budget, is a step finance directors across the sector would recognise as a last-resort funding route.
findings.figures: £18.4 million (gap identified in 2026/27); £0.934 million (surplus forecast in the February 2025 MTFS for 2025/26); £2.938 million (quarter two 2025/26 forecast overspend)
findings.quote: it has applied to the Government for approval of Exceptional Financial Support (EFS)
